paper_metadata.title: Microstructure and mechanical properties of Nb–Mo–ZrB2 composites prepared by hot-pressing sintering
paper_metadata.journal: International Journal of Minerals, Metallurgy and Materials

evidence.quote: Nb–Mo–ZrB2 composites (V(Nb)/V(Mo) = 1) with 15vol% or 30vol% of ZrB2 were fabricated by hot-pressing sintering at 2000°C.
For comparison, Nb−Mo alloy without ZrB2 (named NM) was also prepared under the same conditions.
The obtained Nb–Mo–ZrB2 composites with 15vol% ZrB2 and 30vol% ZrB2 were denoted as NM–15Z and NM–30Z, respectively.

evidence.quote: The improvement in the compressive strength of the Nb–Mo–ZrB2 composites is mainly attributed to the secondary phase strengthening of the stiffer ZrB phase, solid-solution strengthening of the (Nb, Mo)ss matrix as well as fine-grain strengthening.
The hardness of NM (184.1 HV) is higher than that of pure Nb (175 HV) at room temperature owing to solid-solution strengthening.
the grain size in NM–30Z is smaller than that in NM–15Z and the smaller grain size generates larger grain interfaces that increase the strength because of fine-grain strengthening.
the ZrB phase acts as a pinning center in grain boundaries and inhibits the growth of Mo-rich (Nb, Mo)ss
The distributed ZrB along grain boundaries acts as pinning centers that slow the slipping of dislocations and improves the mechanical properties.
the pores and holes in the samples initiate cracks during compressive strength testing. As a result, the fracture toughness of NM is the lowest.
the brittle fracture of the secondary phase ZrB is the main reason that decreases the fracture toughness.

the ZrB phase acts as a pinning center in grain boundaries and inhibits the growth of Mo-rich (Nb, Mo)ss, increasing the strength and fracture toughness because of second-phase dispersion strengthening and fine-grain strengthening.
The distributed ZrB along grain boundaries acts as pinning centers that slow the slipping of dislocations and improves the mechanical properties.
It is reasonable to argue that ZrB2 is a reinforcing phase in Nb–Mo–ZrB2 composites based on secondary phase dispersion strengthening.
